slides.body: <<<INDENT>>>The fullback position is vital to the unique and sustained success of the offense OC Brian Fleury is attempting to implement for our beloved Seattle Seahawks. slides.title: Chicago Bears Question of the Day: Will injuries in the secondary derail the season?
slides.body: <<<INDENT>>>n I’ve been trying to argue on behalf of the Chicago Bears’ secondary for three seasons now. There is just too much talent to ignore. This year, Jaylon Johnson, Kyler Gordon, Coby Bryant, Dillon Thieneman, Tyrique Stevenson, Malik Muhammad, Terrell Smith, and Cam Lewis are a formidable group. Throw in the likes of past Bears Kevin Byard, Jaquan Brisker, Nashon Wright, and more and the Bears have been swarming in talent over the last few years.

<<<INDENT>>>(cont) Despite leading the league in takeaways last season, it still felt like the secondary over the last few seasons has been underperforming. A lot of that is due to persisting injuries to important talents. The 2026 offseason has not been kind to this unit so far, either.

slides.title: OC Matt Nagy: Giants only ‘halfway through’ installing their offense
slides.body: <<<INDENT>>>More often than not throughout the early stages of New York Giants training camp, the defense has gotten the better of the offense during team periods. That is cause for alarm among some on the fan base . There are many who did not like the hiring of Matt Nagy as offensive coordinator, and aren’t sure how the Giants’ offense is going to come together with multiple former head coaches or play callers on the staff.

<<<INDENT>>>(cont) Nagy offered a hint regarding why the offense has not been better during first first media availability of training camp on Tuesday. As Nagy explains it, the offense we are seeing is far from complete, and far from polished. “We’re halfway through camp right now. We have still two and a half weeks. We’re halfway through our run install and halfway through our pass install, if it gives you any perspective,” Nagy said.

slides.title: The Science of “Ramping Up”: Why Aaron Glenn Playing Starters is a Calculated Risk Worth Taking
slides.body: <<<INDENT>>>For years, the conventional wisdom in NFL training camps was simple: wrap the starters in bubble wrap, hold them out of preseason games, save them for Week 1. And every September, like clockwork, the league watches soft-tissue injuries pile up anyway – hamstrings, calves, Achilles, all the non contact stuff that has nothing to do with getting hit and everything to do with a body that wasn’t ready to go full speed. There’s actually a real world test of this. In 2020,

<<<INDENT>>>(cont) the NFL canceled the entire preseason because of COVID. No joint practices, no exhibition games, nothing. Researchers compared that season’s regular season injury numbers to 2018-19 and found soft-tissue injuries jumped hard.

slides.title: SF Giants ride quality pitching, Bryce Eldridge homer to 4-1 victory over Astros
slides.body: <<<INDENT>>>Winning a close game where the Giants ran the bases opportunistically and the other team committed a bunch of errors? That’s some weird, wild stuff. Carson Whisenhunt had a rough start, letting six of the first nine Astros he faced reach base. But he escaped and eventually earned his third win of the season after giving up just one run in 5.2 innings. Then Carson Seymour came through with two shutout innings of relief, yielding only a single to “Late Night” LaMonte Wade, Jr.

<<<INDENT>>>(cont) It was a different sort of game for the Giants, who continued their hard-luck ways Monday when Andrew Susac fouled a ball off leg and fractured his kneecap, which will keep him off the field and off his scooter for the foreseeable future. But Tuesday, the breaks started to go their way. In the first inning, Whisenhunt escaped a bases-loaded jam, caused by a walk, a single and hitting Jose Altuve with a pitch.

slides.title: Astros Waste Early Opportunities in 4-1 Loss to Giants
slides.body: <<<INDENT>>>Not only would Houston lose by a score of 4-1, but they’d also witness an early exit from Jose Altuve who was hit in the left foot on an errant pitch from Carson Whisenhunt during his first AB. slides.title: In the lab: An alternative look at offensive efficiency
slides.body: <<<INDENT>>>One of the more fascinating parts of statistics is that they give us the opportunity to prove or disprove the veracity of what we are seeing and experiencing. Games like last night come immediately to the forefront. The Astros load the bases twice in the first two innings with a combined one out and come up with only one run. It often feels like the Astros leave a small village on base. That speaks to offensive efficiency and we have covered that ground before. <<<INDENT>>>(cont) It wouldn’t surprise anyone to see that the Astros efficiency rating has gone up this year as they have scored more runs and generally had more offensive success.

slides.title: Ranking MLB teams by World Series titles: Which clubs have never won?
slides.body: <<<INDENT>>>Every February, all 30 MLB franchises begin spring training with a renewed sense of hope. Their bodies are rested, their eyes already on the fall with the dream of hoisting the Commissioner's Trophy as World Series champions. It's an exclusive club . . . but not as exclusive as you might expect. All in all, 25 out of 30 big league franchises have won at least one championship. Out of the five who have yet to win one, <<<INDENT>>>(cont) only the Seattle Mariners have yet to appear in a World Series.

slides.title: Tigers seek series-clinching win over Guardians on Wednesday night
slides.body: <<<INDENT>>>The Detroit Tigers took the first game of a critical home series against the Cleveland Guardians on Tuesday night with a narrow 6-4 victory. The good guys got their first win against Tanner Bibee since July 2024 thanks to some well-timed offense, and somehow, Kenley Jansen did not blow the save despite feeding the batters meatballs in the ninth. Taking the mound for the Motor City Kitties in Game 2 is left-hander Framber Valdez, who is coming off two straight seven-

<<<INDENT>>>(cont) inning quality starts. Across those 14 frames of work, the 32-year-old veteran posted a 1.29 ERA and 2.38 FIP on 14 hits and four walks — good for a 1.29 WHIP — while striking out 11 en route to a pair of wins. Valdez faced Cleveland once before this season on May 18 in Detroit, and it was not pretty, serving up four runs on five hits and four walks while striking out three over five innings of work to take the L in an 8-2 loss.

slides.title: Orioles news: Alonso, Henderson power O’s to big win
slides.body: <<<INDENT>>>For whatever reason, the O’s bats are able to provide run support when Young is on the mound, and they did so again on Tuesday night. Getting shut out for the final six innings is bad. That is the 2026 Orioles experience in a nutshell. But on this night, <<<INDENT>>>(cont) it was good enough for the win.
